s1.syndrome_frame: Acute collapse with recurrent episodes of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation
salient_findings: Repetitive monomorphic premature ventricular complexes with atypical left bundle-branch block morphology
Recurrent episodes of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 50s
Collapsed at home and received chest compressions from her husband
Recovered consciousness at home
Vital signs were normal on admission
Physical examination was unremarkable
ECG showed sinus rhythm with normal QRS and QT intervals
ECG showed repetitive monomorphic premature ventricular complexes
Short-coupling interval of 240 milliseconds
Continuous ECG monitoring revealed recurrent episodes of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
Some episodes deteriorated into ventricular fibrillation
Serum electrolyte levels were normal
Transthoracic echocardiography showed normal cardiac function and structure
Emergency coronary angiography showed no evidence of obstructive coronary artery disease
Genetic testing revealed a variant of unknown significance in the coding gene of cardiac ryanodine receptor (RyR2)

shortlist.label: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent episodes of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation, normal cardiac structure and function, and genetic variant of unknown significance in the coding gene of cardiac ryanodine receptor (RyR2)

shortlist.label: Idiopathic ventricular fibrillation
shortlist.why_kept: Normal cardiac structure and function, normal serum electrolyte levels, and absence of obstructive coronary artery disease

shortlist.label: Early repolarization syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Repetitive monomorphic premature ventricular complexes with atypical left bundle-branch block morphology and short-coupling interval

shortlist.label: Ryanodine receptor type 2 mutation
shortlist.why_kept: Genetic variant of unknown significance in the coding gene of cardiac ryanodine receptor (RyR2) and recurrent episodes of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia

shortlist.label: Short-coupled polymorphic ventricular tachycardia/ventricular fibrillation
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent episodes of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation, short-coupling interval of 240 milliseconds, and normal cardiac structure and function

raw.rationale: The patient's ECG showed repetitive monomorphic premature ventricular complexes with a short-coupling interval of 240 milliseconds, which is consistent with short-coupled polymorphic ventricular tachycardia/ventricular fibrillation (SC-PMVT/VF). The patient's episodes of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
rejected.why: The vignette does not mention any triggers or symptoms suggestive of catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT), such as exercise or emotional stress.

rejected.label: Idiopathic ventricular fibrillation
rejected.why: The patient's ECG findings, including repetitive monomorphic premature ventricular complexes, are more specific for SC-PMVT/VF than idiopathic ventricular fibrillation.

rejected.label: Early repolarization syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's ECG does not show the characteristic J-point elevation or ST-segment elevation seen in early repolarization syndrome.

rejected.label: Ryanodine receptor type 2 mutation
rejected.why: While the patient has a variant of unknown significance in the coding gene of cardiac ryanodine receptor (RyR2), this is not sufficient to make a diagnosis of a RyR2 mutation-related condition without further evidence or family history.
